sentences.text: 2. MFA No.546/2018 is filed by the respondent and the MFA No.6035/2018 is filed by the petitioner before the Tribunal.

3. The petitioner contends that while he was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA.50.K.2262 from Kodigehalli towards Bhadrappa Layout, near Indus Steel Shop, Tata Nagar, Bangalore, the rider of Bullet Motor cycle bearing No.KA.03.HS.7511 came from opposite direction and without observing any rules or regulations or giving any indication took a sudden right turn and dashed to the motors cycle of the petitioner causing the accident.

The petitioner fell down and sustained fracture of the upper NC: 2023:KHC:21582 end of right tibia and he was shifted to Sri Sai Northside hospital,
Bengaluru.
He had to take treatment for 6 days and the injury was treated with locking plate fixation under a surgical procedure.
Contending that he has sustained permanent disability and that he was working in Prakash Hallow Bricks and earning `15,000/- per month, he claimed an adequate compensation from the respondents.
It was also contended that a case was registered by the Hebbala Traffic police in Crime 120/2016 against the respondent and ultimately chargesheet was filed against him.

4. On issuance of notice, the respondent, who is the owner of the bullet motor cycle appeared before the Tribunal and filed objections contending that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, imaginary, exaggerated, excessive and fanciful and that the accident was due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
It was admitted that as on NC: 2023:KHC:21582 the date of the accident there was no insurance policy in force.
5. On the basis of the pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues and the petitioner was examined as PW1 and a Doctor was examined as PW2
, Exs.P1 to P20 were marked.

The respondent was examined as RW1.
6.
After hearing both the sides, the Tribunal awarded a sum of `5,85,000/- under following heads and also held that the petitioner had contributed 50% towards the negligence.

Pain and sufferings ` 1,00,000/-
 Loss of future income ` 2,74,176/-
Loss of Income during laid of period ` 24,000/-
 - 12000x2  Loss of amenities ` 15,000/-
 Medical expenses ` 1,01,691/-
 Future surgery ` 50,000/-
 Conveyance, food & Nourishment ` 20,000/-

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner has approached this Court in MFA No.6035/2018 contending that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC:21582 is inadequate and low and fastening contributory negligence and the liability to the extent of 50% on him is erroneous.
Whereas, the respondent has approached this Court in MFA No.546/2018 contending that the compensation awarded is on the higher side and that fastening of 50% of liability on him is incorrect.
8. On issuance of notice in both the appeals, the rival parties have appeared through their counsel.
9. The Tribunal records have been secured and the arguments by both the sides are heard.
10. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contend that there was no contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner and the Tribunal has erred in fastening 50% negligence on him.
He has referred to the police papers, particularly, the spot mahazar and the sketch of the spot.
He also contended that the compensation awarded is low and the functional disability has not been properly assessed by the Tribunal.

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent contended that the Tribunal fell in error in holding that the petitioner was earning `12,000/- per month and no acceptable evidence was placed before the Tribunal.
He also contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and also that entire negligence should have been attributed to the petitioner.

12. The perusal of the Tribunal records, particularly, the Ex.P3-sketch and Ex.P4-Panchanama would show that the accident had happened on Kodigehhalli Bhadrappa Layout road and the spot of the accident is at the junction of the 5th Cross, Tatanagar road.
It is evident that the petitioner was going towards Bhadrappa Layout and he was on his left side.
He had crossed the cross road towards Narayanappa layout and had come infront of the 5th Cross Road junction.
The line of motion of the bullet motor cycle of the respondent show that, he came on the right side and he did not slow down his vehicle.
The NC: 2023:KHC:21582 contention of the respondent is that, he had to take a right turn to go to Narayanappa Layout and he had put on his indicators.

Even if we accept the contention of the respondent, it is evident that he could have taken the right turn after approaching the 'T'
junction of Narayanappa layout and his taking right turn was much prior to approaching the Narayanappa Layout Cross.
More over, the police papers also indicate that the entire negligence was fastened upon the respondent.
Obviously, the petitioner was on the left side of the road and he had crossed the Narayanappa Layout Cross.

Therefore, it is obvious that the Tribunal did not consider this aspect of the matter.
13.

Another factor to be noticed is that when the respondent had seen the motor cycle of the petitioner coming from the opposite direction on his right side, he should have given the way for the motor cycle of the petitioner and then should have taken the right turn.

4 laid down that the vehicle coming NC: 2023:KHC:21582 from the right ought to be given priority.
This requirement was flouted by the respondent.
Hence, in the considered opinion of this Court, the gravity of the actionable negligence on the part of the petitioner was much lesser than that of the respondent.
Consequently, the negligence of the petitioner is held to be 25% and that of the respondent is 75%.
14. The perusal of the evidence shows that though the petitioner has produced salary certificate at Ex.P14, but he has not examined the author of Ex.P14 in order to establish his income conclusively.
In fact, Ex.P14 is a letter addressed to no one.
Hence, the veracity of Ex.P14 is not established.
Consequently, Ex.P14 was rightly rejected by the Tribunal.
When Ex.P14 is rejected, the next consequence was to consider the notional income.
No reasons are assigned by the Tribunal to hold that the petitioner had the income of `12,000/- per month.

The guidelines issued by the KSLSA in respect of the notional income for settlement of disputes before the Lok Adalat - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:21582 prescribe `9,500/- per month as the notional income for the year 2016.
Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered to be `9,500/- per month.
15. PW2 in his evidence before the Tribunal has stated that there is a disability of 13.6% to the lower limb and the Tribunal has accepted such disability.
Since the petitioner is stated to be working in a Hallow Bricks factory as a Supervisor, definitely, there would be an impairment in his functional capacity.
This Court do not see any reason to hold that the observations of the Tribunal regarding the disability are erroneous or misplaced.
16. The petitioner is aged 43 years and therefore the appropriate multiplier would be '14'.

Hence, the loss of future income is calculated as `9,500/- x 12 x 14 x 13.6% =`2,17,056/-.
17.
As a consequence, the loss of income during the laid up period also needs to be revised.
The Tribunal has considered the laid up period to be two months which is inadequate as the injury is to the lower limb.
Hence, the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:21582 loss of income for the laid up period for three months is calculated at `28,500/-.
18. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `15,000/- towards loss of amenities and the same needs to be enhanced to `20,000/-.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of pain and sufferings is to the tune of `1,00,000/-.
There was only one fracture and therefore, the same needs to be reduced to `40,000/-.
The compensation awarded under the heads of medical expenses, future medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment, do not require any modification.

Hence, the compensation is reassessed as below:
 Pain and sufferings ` 40,000/-

Out of total compensation of `4,77,247/-, the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner being - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:21582 25%, the entitlement of the petitioner comes to `3,57,935/-
(4,77,247-1,19,311).
19. For the aforesaid reasons, the appeals are to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following :
ORDER (i) Both the appeals are allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
The contributory negligence of the petitioner is held to be 25%.

(iii) The compensation is re-assessed at `4,77,247/- and the petitioner having contributed 25% of the negligence, he is entitled for `3,57,935/- from the respondent along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its deposit.
(iv) The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within period of two months from the date of this order.
(v) In the event of deposit, the entire amount be released to the petitioner.
(vi) The amount in deposit in MFA No.546/2018 shall be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.
